draft.title: Promotion techniques
card: Advertising
paid messages in media such as TV, radio, print and online. The business controls what is said and where it appears.
Social media and influencers
posts, videos and pages on social platforms, including people with large followings who feature a product.
Sales promotion
short-term offers that encourage a quick purchase, such as discounts, free samples, competitions and loyalty points.
Personal selling
a salesperson speaks with a customer directly, answers questions and helps them choose. Publicity is unpaid media coverage of a business, such as a news story about a new store.
draft.remember: Businesses can mix paid messages, online content, special offers, face-to-face selling and media coverage to reach customers.

a.q: A shoe shop in Parramatta offers 30% off all sandals for one weekend only. Which technique is this?
a.why: A discount that runs for a short time to prompt a quick purchase is a sales promotion. Advertising is a paid message in the media. The offer is not advertising in itself, even though the shop may advertise it.
a.clue: Think about a short-term offer that encourages buying now.

b.q: A local newspaper writes a story about Ava's new bakery in Orange after a reporter visited. Ava did not pay for it. What is this?
b.why: Unpaid media coverage of a business is publicity. It is tempting to call it advertising because it appears in the media, but advertising is paid for and the business controls the message.

problems.detail: Publicity is defined inside the 'Personal selling' bullet, so a student could read it as a kind of personal selling. It needs its own bullet.
The clue 'a short-term offer that encourages buying now' repeats the card's definition of sales promotion almost word for word. A student can match it to the answer without understanding the idea.
